by.quote: Glosses inside spoken dialogue ("shodan (first dan)", "tsuka (hilt)", "水 (Wednesday)"). On a voiced line, the parentheses break the rhythm of the English text. ... A margin note or translator's footnote style would sit better than a mid-line gloss.

items.why: Touches the shodan gloss and even suggests translator's notes, but complains about rhythm, not that the foods/terms need more explanation; no check flags karaage, kinpira, taiyaki, miso or fusuma as unclear.

by.quote: c1_0227 "Natsuki laughed first. The moment closed up, and it was fine." FLAT (explains itself). It narrates the laugh-close the reader just watched. c1_0228 "It was fine." carries the irony alone.

items.why: Same line, same problem (narration vouching for the moment) for c1_0227; diagnosis would keep c1_0228, which the author also cut.

by.quote: Height gags. Five: c1_0040, c1_0043, c1_0075, c1_0127 ("elbow height") and "Chibi" at c1_0256. "Short-person direction" and "Chibi" are required, so drop c1_0075 and the joke stops being milked.
She's also supposed to be "up on her toes"; her feet are out of frame, so it doesn't read.
her feet are cropped, so the on-her-toes beat isn't visible. Not wrong, but the "she's needed the extra inches" line has nothing to land on in the picture.
"up on her toes" and the height joke aren't supported by the art. ... It's minor, but the joke depends on her being small and she doesn't look especially small here.

items.why: Diagnosis names the same overplayed height joke at c1_0075/c1_0127; readers touch c1_0074–c1_0075 only as text/art mismatches.

by.quote: In a short span it has the cardigan, the uniform "ironed by someone who meant it," "elbow height," his hand that's "betrayed me," the weathervane, and the good rice. Each is fine alone, but together they give a punchline-every-paragraph rhythm ... Trim two or three.

items.why: Points at the line but as one of several quips in a density problem and says each is fine alone, not that this line fails to land.
No check notes the missing class reaction to Natsuki's looks; diagnosis's c1_0144 flag asks to remove the class reaction to her joke, not to add one.

by.quote: Neat buttons. Almost every comic exchange ends on a capper: ... "That's what it says in the minutes" → "two points" → "You're losing"

items.why: Touches the banter's ending only as an example of capper rhythm; all three readers praised the exchange as the chapter's best.
